title: Tool handoff handshake and stream-framing guards for multi-tool chains
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we increase multi-tool chaining and streaming function calls from the Core API, we've observed two classes of production failures: (1) uncontrolled recursive loops / inadvertent repeated invocations when tools return text that triggers another tool, and (2) stream framing and partial-result ambiguity when tool outputs are injected mid-stream, causing consumers to receive interleaved structured tokens and free text that violate downstream parsers.

Goal: Design and implement a handshake and framing protocol that: (a) enforces a lightweight tool-handoff handshake to confirm intent and idempotency tokens before executing downstream tools, (b) establishes clear stream chunk framing for injected tool results (structured boundary markers + schema version) so streaming consumers can parse deterministically, and (c) integrates runtime loop/recursion guards that detect call-graph cycles, enforce soft limits, and provide deterministic fallback behavior.

Scope: runtime executor + API surface for tool/function calls + streaming path + compatibility layer for older tool adapters. Not in scope: changes to third-party partner tools; those will be handled via adapters in the compatibility layer.
acceptance_criteria: When a chain includes >=2 tool invocations, the executor must perform a short handshake (intent token exchange) and attach an idempotency fingerprint to each tool call.

Streaming responses that include injected tool results must include explicit framing markers ("<<TOOL_START v=1 id=...>>" / "<<TOOL_END id=...>>") and a schema_version field so clients can reliably extract structured outputs.

A recursive call graph detector must trigger a deterministic fallback: cancel the downstream tool and emit a structured error block into the stream with reason=recursion_limit and guidance for the client.
Compatibility layer maps legacy tool adapters (pre-framing) into the new handshake/framing protocol without requiring adapter rewrites; conversion logs emitted for audit.

Telemetry: new metrics available in console - tool_handoffs_total, handshakes_failed, recursion_guard_tripped, stream_frame_parse_errors. Dashboards and alerting (SLO thresholds) configured in the release window.
E2E tests simulate a chain with mocked legacy adapters and verify parseability of streamed output and that recursion guards prevent infinite cycles under load.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Handshake: before executing Tool B triggered by Tool A, the executor generates an intent token (hash of request id + call-site fingerprint + timestamp) and sends it to the downstream tool adapter. The adapter must echo the token in its initial ACK. If ACK not received within handshake_timeout (configurable default 250ms), proceed only if the adapter is marked 'best-effort'; otherwise abort with structured error. This protects against accidental replays and partial injection loops.

2) Idempotency: attach a short idempotency_fingerprint to tool invocations (sha1 of call-signature) so retries or duplicate events can be deduplicated at the adapter/runtime layer. Store recent fingerprints in a time-windowed in-memory LRU (configurable TTL, default 30s) per request shard.

3) Stream framing: define read-friendly markers for injected tool results. Each injected segment will be wrapped with an opening marker containing id, schema_version, and a provenance signature, followed by JSON-encoded structured payload or plain text, and closed with the matching end marker. Consumers that don't understand framing or older SDKs will receive a compatibility-mode wrapper (base64 + envelope) produced by the compatibility layer.

4) Recursion detection: maintain a lightweight call graph per top-level request (call-site fingerprints only). If a repeated fingerprint is observed beyond recursion_threshold (default 3 occurrences) within a sliding window (default 60s), mark the chain as recursive and trigger fallback: cancel the newest invocation, emit structured error block into stream, and increment recursion metric. For long-lived streams, issue periodic heartbeats to clear old fingerprints to avoid false positives.

5) Compatibility: provide an adapter shim that wraps legacy tool adapters that only return concatenated text. The shim will attempt to parse structured tokens heuristically (using delimiter heuristics) and, failing that, wrap the returned payload in a framed envelope with schema_version=legacy-0. The shim emits a conversion log entry and increments a telemetry counter.

Security considerations: provenance signature must use per-tenant HMAC key (from KMS) for hosted and dedicated deployments; for private deployments, keys are provided or the feature can be disabled. Avoid signing large payloads — sign metadata only.

Tradeoffs: handshake adds ~0.2-1.5% latency on short chains; prevents harder-to-debug recursive behavior. Framing increases payload by markers but gives deterministic parsing. The compatibility shim reduces friction for partners at cost of added complexity and conversion logs.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): prover handshake + idempotency window + unit tests + adapter shim prototype.
Phase 2 (2 sprints): stream framing markers + SDK parsing helpers for JS/Py + compatibility layer integration + e2e tests.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): recursion detector + telemetry + rollout canary and dashboards.
Phase 4 (1 sprint): privacy/security audit and optional per-tenant KMS integration for provenance signatures.

Milestones with owners: handshake core (Liam R.), adapter shim (Chen W.), framing + SDK helpers (Aisha K.), recursion detector + metrics (Riley Nguyen), canary + dashboards (Product/Observability).
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake timeout, idempotency dedupe, and marker generation. Integration tests: simulated chain with three tools, where tool B triggers tool C and C returns structured JSON mid-stream. Backstop test: an intentionally recursive chain that would previously loop indefinitely - must be truncated and emit structured error. Load test: 1000 concurrent chained requests with streaming enabled; verify recursion guard false-positive rate < 0.1%. SDK parser tests across JS/Py versions and legacy-compat mode.
rollout_plan:
Canary: enable framing+handshake for 5% of hosted-API traffic targeting non-critical accounts for 72h. Monitor handshakes_failed and stream_frame_parse_errors. If thresholds breached (>0.5% errors or >0.1% latency regression), rollback.
Gradual: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with rolling migrations for Dedicated customers coordinated with account leads.
Private: ship as opt-in in runtime-2.3; recommend customers enable in a testing environment first. Provide feature flag toggles.
Docs: update API docs with new framing spec, SDK helper snippets, and migration guide for legacy adapters.
telemetry_and_alerting:
New metrics: tool_handoff_handshake_total, tool_handoff_handshake_time_ms_p50/p95, handshake_timeouts, idempotency_dedupe_count, recursion_guard_trips, stream_frame_parse_errors, compatibility_shim_conversions.
Dashboards: per-model and per-tenant breakdown of handshake latencies and parse errors.
Alerts: page if handshake_timeouts_rate > 0.5% over 5m for production tier or recursion_guard_trips spike > 10x baseline.
Logs: structured conversion logs for shim events stored (retention 30d) with search tags: tenant_id, request_id, adapter_name.
migration_notes:
Adapter authors: two paths: (1) adopt handshake + framing (preferred) by implementing minimal ACK behavior and emitting frame markers, or (2) continue as legacy and rely on shim which will wrap outputs. Provide a migration checklist and sample shim implementation in repo under rlin/runtime/adapters/shims.
Offer a compatibility test harness (local) so adapter teams can verify they return correctly framed outputs.
Communicate to top 20 customers two weeks before enabling canary and provide rollback contacts.
risks: Increased tail latency for short chains due to handshake timeouts — mitigate with adaptive timeout tuning.
False-positive recursion detection for high fanout workflows — mitigate by increasing window and using call-site entropy in fingerprinting.
SDK adoption lag: older clients may not parse framed streams; need to ensure compatibility-mode is robust.
KMS integration for provenance increases operational complexity for Private deployments; provide opt-out.
